Perditaj knew he was different. The other Spectra always said that when they were around him they felt like the Crystal Tower was near. Even when Perditaj was far from the tower, which was more and more frequent as spasms of pain wracked him on occasion when he was near.

A lot of spectra thought he might have been born from the Tower itself, or perhaps whatever lay beyond the rift in its core. But when he had visited the rift, he found that he couldn't fit through, so how could he have come from it? No, he must have been born from something else. But what?

Most spectra didn't bother trying to find their origin. But Perditaj felt out of place. Beyond his effect on anyone who got close, he had lost concentration on several occasions. But he had survived, simply floating through objects until he could force himself to take shape as a spectrus again. Normally, losing focus was fatal. But he survived it. Why?

His constant questioning had driven him to the Order of The Moon, but he had found that they were turned outward, always asking about others and never about themselves, while he was the subject he was most curious about.

He found himself taking longer and longer drifts around the outskirts of Sentenza, drifting sometimes over the water. Then, on on calm day, he looked down, and got a clear view of his reflection.

Several researches looked up, annoyed, as Perditaj came rushing into the complex holding a goblet of water. "Look at it!" He shouted. "What do you see!"

Most simply turned back to their work and ignored him. A few came over and looked at their reflections in the glass, but none reacted with surprise. Soon, they had all gone, laughing quietly ad Perditaj's apparent delusions. Perditaj would need to do something more noticeable. Peering into his reflection, he saw the same thing he had seen before; a strange, undescribable being, using the Spectra body like a puppet. Thinking back to the times when he had lost form, and to before he had a shape, he remembered what that felt like. Casting about his mind, he found a little bit that was always asking "How does a spectra react to this wind/gravity/light?" Then, he shut that bit off.

*****

Perditaj had definitely gotten some attention like that, but he wasn't sure he liked it. He was back in Spectra form, which he was most used to, but that was only a fancy. Any form he took, he moved in like he was born to it. The best the Order could tell he was some sort of mimic being, probably related to the Reflected Images that wandered the wilderness. But he wasn't identical, he could change his size within limits and could remember classes of being or individuals (being another spectra had been very weird) without having to see them constantly.

He was something new, something deviant. He didn't know whether the spectra would still consider him one of them, though he definitely still thought of himself as one. He didn't know if there were any others like him. And he didn't know what would come next.
